name: orb_failure_trade_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Failed ORB breakouts — where price breaks above the 15-min ORB high but then reverses back below ORB_high within 15 bars — are high-probability reversal signals. The failure indicates that breakout buyers are trapped and will be forced to liquidate, creating selling pressure that drives price back through the ORB range and often toward the opposite extreme. Failed breakouts have a 55-60% probability of reaching the ORB midpoint and ~45% probability of reaching the opposite ORB extreme. The inefficiency exists because most traders cut their loss on the failed breakout and don't realize that the failure itself is a higher-probability trade in the opposite direction. Trapped traders' forced liquidation creates reliable flow for the contrarian.
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹200cr; ORB breakout occurred and then failed within 15 bars
indicators: breakout_failed_up = breakout_occurred_up AND close < ORB_high_15 (price back inside range)
bars_since_breakout = count bars since last ORB level cross

conditions: breakout_failed_down == True (price broke below ORB_low then came back above it)
RSI_14 > 40 (momentum turning positive after false breakdown)
long.confirmation: close > ORB_low_15 for 2 consecutive bars (not a momentary whipsaw)

conditions: breakout_failed_up == True (price broke above ORB_high then came back below it)
RSI_14 < 60 (momentum turning negative after false breakout)

entry.entry_price: market order on 2nd consecutive bar back inside ORB range

exit.target: opposite ORB extreme (ORB_high for failed-down longs, ORB_low for failed-up shorts)
exit.stop_loss: price re-breaks the failed level (new high beyond breakout high for failed-up shorts) OR 0.4 * ORB_range beyond ORB extreme
exit.trailing_stop: after reaching ORB_mid, trail stop at ORB extreme where failure occurred
exit.signal_exit: if price makes a new extreme beyond the failed breakout level (re-break), exit immediately

filters.time_filter: failures must occur between 09:30-10:00 IST (within first 30 min of ORB formation); enter on failure confirmation
filters.volume_filter: breakout bar had high volume (> 1.5x avg) AND failure bar has rising volume (trapped traders liquidating)
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY direction opposite to the failed breakout direction (macro context supports the reversal)
filters.event_filter: skip if breakout was driven by stock-specific news (failure may be temporary before continuation)
other_filters: failure must occur within 15 bars; slow failures (16+ bars) are more likely consolidation, not reversal

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — failed breakout trading is psychologically difficult (buying after just seeing a breakdown), which limits crowding

weaknesses: Distinguishing a genuine failed breakout from a brief re-test that will re-break is extremely difficult; many 'failures' are just pauses before continuation
The strategy enters AFTER the breakout AND the failure, meaning entry is often 5-10 bps worse than the original ORB level due to the round-trip price action
On strong trend days, what appears as a failed breakout in one direction is actually a setup for a massive breakout in the original direction — the failure is the trap
prior_art: Brooks (2009) 'Reading Price Charts Bar by Bar' on failed breakouts; Bulkowski (2005) on chart pattern failures. Similar to Adam Grimes (2012) concept of 'failed patterns as signals'.
notes: Edge math: 0.58 * 55bps - 0.42 * 30bps = 31.9 - 12.6 = 19.3bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~10.3bps/trade * 1.5 trades = ~15.5bps daily. The 30bps estimate includes occasional failed breakouts that drive price all the way through to the opposite ORB extreme (full range traversal = 80+ bps).
